title: Three darknesses
hook: in the night, in the sea, inside the fish, Yunus calls out: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong
tomorrow: the gourd and the saved city

segments.voice: Yesterday, Yunus left his people in anger and ended up in the sea. Your line was walking away is also a choice. Did you catch yourself about to flee? Day seventy-six.

Have you ever been somewhere truly dark? Not a room with the lights off. The kind of dark where you hold your hand in front of your face and there's nothing. Now stack it. It's night. Under the night, the sea. Under the sea, inside a great fish, a man. Early commentators called it three darknesses: the dark of the night, the dark of the water, the dark of the belly of the fish. No ship. No crew. No one who could possibly hear him. And the man who walked out on his people in anger now has nowhere left to walk. And in there, he says something.
screen: `THE DARK OF THE NIGHT.` → `THE DARK OF THE SEA.` → `THE DARK OF THE FISH.`

segments.voice: Surah Al-Anbiya says he cried out in the darkness. And here is his prayer, in Pickthall's translation: “There is no God save Thee. Be Thou glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer.” In Arabic: la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu mina z-zalimin. Three short pieces. Look at each one. First, la ilaha illa anta: there is no god but You. That's tawhid, day ten of this path, but said face to face. Not about Allah, to Him. Second, subhanaka: glory to You. You are beyond all this, above any fault. Third, and hardest: I was one of the wrongdoers. No excuse. No mention of how stubborn his people were. He doesn't say, they drove me to it. He says, I was wrong. You've heard that shape before on this path. Adam and Hawwa: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. Musa after the blow: my Lord, I have wronged myself. The prophets keep saying it. And then the next verse: “Then we heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish. Thus we save believers.” Notice that last line. Thus we save believers. Not just Yunus. The Qur'an turns the story outward. And a hadith in Tirmidhi says that the prayer of Dhu n-Nun, whenever a Muslim calls with it for anything, is answered. Which is why so many Muslims know these words by heart, and say them in their own dark places: in a hospital corridor, in debt, at three in the morning. Another surah adds that if Yunus had not been one who glorified Allah, he would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the day of rising.
screen: `LA ILAHA ILLA ANTA: NO GOD BUT YOU.` · `SUBHANAKA: GLORY TO YOU.` · `I HAVE BEEN A WRONG-DOER.` · `WE HEARD HIS PRAYER AND SAVED HIM.` · then, large: `THUS WE SAVE BELIEVERS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Close your eyes and let it be dark. If you pray, say the prayer of Yunus slowly, three times, silently or in a whisper: la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu mina z-zalimin. There is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong. Leave a breath between each piece. If you don't pray, simply listen to the words in your mind, and let the last one land: I was wrong. Notice what it's like to say it without an excuse. The bell holds the time.
Three darknesses. The night, the sea and the fish, where Yunus called: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong.

Your line: la ilaha illa anta. There is no god but You. Today, when you find yourself in a dark moment, say it once, or just remember that Yunus did. Tomorrow, what happened when he came out. Day seventy-six.

screen: `DAY 76 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE GOURD AND THE SAVED CITY.`

howItsDone: Many Muslims say the prayer of Yunus, la ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu mina z-zalimin, in times of distress, sometimes repeating it many times, trusting the hadith that it is answered.

fork.setup: Yunus is in the dark, inside the fish, with no one to hear. what does he say?
options: why did You let this happen to me?
there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong.
fork.reveal: there is no God save Thee. be Thou glorified! lo! I have been a wrong-doer (21:87). and the next verse: we heard his prayer.

original.script: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
original.say: laa i-LAA-ha il-LAA AN-ta, sub-HAA-na-ka, IN-nee KUN-tu mi-naz-zaa-li-MEEN
original.note: Arabic, Qur'an 21:87: the prayer of Yunus in the dark.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man trapped in a whale says sorry.
what it means: in the deepest dark, Yunus says three things: only You, glory to You, I was wrong. and he is heard.
what a scholar hears: the three darknesses come from early commentators on 21:87; and 37:143–144 adds that without his glorifying he would have stayed in the fish until the day of rising.
